name: Korah
overview: Korah was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified as the son of Hebron. His lineage is noted in 1 Chronicles 2:43, which situates him within the genealogical records of Israel. Beyond his tribal affiliation and paternal connection, no additional personal notes are recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Korah means 'shaven' or 'bald' in Hebrew, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 2:43. This is the only name attributed to him and does not carry specific divine origin or additional titles.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Korah as the son of Hebron. It is also inferred that Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema are his fathers, suggesting a broader family context mentioned in the same verse. No further family details are provided beyond these relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Korah is significant in the biblical narrative as a Levite who led a rebellion against the divinely appointed leadership of Moses and Aaron. His challenge to God's established priesthood and authority resulted in severe judgment, underscoring the importance of respecting God's chosen leaders. This episode serves as a solemn warning against pride and disputing God's order within His covenant people.

keyEvents.event: Led rebellion against Moses and Aaron
